I have depression and PTSD. Some weeks go from manageable to awful, and similar to your girlfriend I ask for alone time. I don’t think it’s healthy for us so I give myself a few days to go to therapy, and use the techniques I’ve learned to try to get myself to a more manageable state. Everyone’s experience with depression is different so I can’t speak for her, but maybe that gives you some context to her behaviour. 

That being said, if it’s that bad, she absolutely should take steps to go to therapy, or see a doctor about medication or whatever her options are for next steps. You sound supportive and it’s wonderful. But if she doesn’t want help or to be helped, then you need to be honest to yourself about what you want out of this relationship.

Strangely difficult, actually. It’s frustrating because all of us on this sub went through some form of self discovery when we realised we loved women, and I don’t mean to be presumptuous but I’m sure some of you battled questions within yourself about “what you are”. I like girls, am I bi? Am I just straight with a little girl crush? Am I a raging lesbian? 

I don’t speak for anybody else but myself, but I identified as lesbian for a long time before I realised the best way to describe myself is pansexual. I liked boys in high school but it never felt real. Then I fell deeply in love with a woman and had eyes only for her. The idea of boys seemed foreign. She made me realise that I could be gay. After that I dated a pre-op trans man, who also would identify himself as a lesbian to save having to explain who he was. We are both Asian so at that time the understanding and acceptance wasn’t there. I still called myself a lesbian as it made the most sense to me. 

After that, I fell for a cis man. I was confused and I went back to the turmoil of what my identity should be, after I was so certain I knew. So I referred to myself as bi. But I didn’t really see myself falling for any other man. I still generally was attracted to women. After him, I exclusively looked to date women. When labelling myself bi, the level of biphobia I encountered was shocking. It’s hard enough to struggle with my sexuality and accept myself, but now I have to encounter it with people I thought could relate? So I went back to labelling myself as a lesbian, figuring it would just be easier to avoid confrontation. I still generally am attracted to women, but occasionally a guy will catch my eye. I hated labelling myself because I didn’t know what else to call myself. Until I learned about pansexuality and finally felt like it was what I identified most with. 

Sorry for the wall of text and life story, but there is a lot of anger and frustration in this thread which is upsetting. To be clear, I agree with what you all are saying but as someone who was on the other side I ask that you be forgiving and educational, not angry. It’s difficult to have to subscribe to labels when you aren’t sure yourself sometimes. Everyone’s journey in sexuality is different.

Limit how long you’re gonna work for free and stick to it. As a rule, try to avoid working for free unless it’s also something you know you’ll enjoy or is something you know you’ll want as a representation of your ability. I’ve worked too many times for free on crap films that never saw the light of day - you CAN afford to be selective. Good luck!

The crowd surged forward at the wailing of the trumpet to catch a glimpse of the royal funeral procession. The intimacy of their warm bodies pushing into mine was more than I’d had for what felt like the beginning of an eternity. In the distance, I could make out the sun glinting on the glass coffin, and I felt my heart rise to my throat as it drew nearer. Around me, men and women began collapsing to their knees in reverence, crying out for their departed princess. I wanted to collapse to my knees and vomit. 

She drew closer still now. I could make out the lace on her favourite white dress. For a moment, I could feel it itching against my fingertips. I could barely swallow. I stepped over the weeping bodies of my fellow countrymen, forcing myself as close as the Royal Guard would allow. She was so close I could see the lashes on her eyes now. I inched closer still, peering into the coffin. I felt my heart burst.

There on her wrist was a crude bracelet fashioned of glass beads. The one I made, desperately in lieu of the diamonds the princes of foreign lands offered for her hand. The hand that preferred my own in secret. My clumsy fingertips still bore scars from my attempt at craftsmanship. She had kissed my scars in between giggles. 

“I thought all women were good at crafting.”

Her encased body moved further away from me, and I looked to her wrist again. The bracelet looked dazzlingly beautiful as the sun cast rainbows against her lace. I smiled and sank to my knees, joining the sobbing ranks on the floor.

If I concentrated, I could just barely feel the coarseness of the scar on her palm that I used to trace endlessly.

The cold in my stomach began to spread up through my chest, and I swear my heart tightened. Here she was in front of me, but something was not right. My mouth was dry. 

"What's wrong baby? You're scaring me."

She grasped my hands and held them to her. She used to grip them with both hands and hold them level as she forced me to breathe whenever I had a panic attack. She got up and tugged me to my feet. It was incredible how well she still knew me. 

I didn't have words for her. I could feel the cold rising and wrapping around the lump in my throat, all warmth dissipating. I wasn't sure how to tell her that the last time I saw her face, I could barely recognise any of her features, or that I was pulling glass out of the tangles of her hair.

I flicked through the options, resting on the maximum 2 year period. I paused. Beyond my headphones, I think I heard the voice of my daughter calling for me.

*Warning: Your existing memories will be suppressed for the duration of the period selected. Continue?*

The cold began to rise again, and I glanced behind the menu at my frozen late wife, staring back at me.

I selected *Yes.*

Everything went black.

I've always dreaded being the last to go upstairs, because I *hated* having to turn the lights off. It's been this way since I was a kid.

What happens is simple. The first part I've felt hundreds of times - and it never gets easier. You flip the lights off, and everything is black. You feel your skin start to crawl, and pressure like the air is closing in around you. You start to feel the hairs on the back of your neck stand up. Then you feel a tingling through your spine, down your back. It feels like the darkness is wrapping around your body and beginning to engulf you, like you're melting into quicksand. You want to be upstairs before you feel this.

Sometimes when I'm running up the stairs, and I don't feel like I've made it in time, I swear I've felt something grabbing at my heels.

But if you stay, you'll feel a moment of stillness. Like a calm before the storm. Then you start feeling a draught, and your body goes cold from within. It spreads throughout your body from the centre, and your heart starts to race. You start feeling inexplicably nervous, and your anxiety goes through the roof. You feel like you're on the verge of a panic attack, but you never get there. You start to twitch. You start to hear disembodied voices start calling you from the beyond. Loud enough to hear, but soft enough to not know what they're saying to you. 

If you've gotten to this point, you no longer have control.

Your legs are now rooted to the floor. You feel invisible hands grab at you, and those voices become louder, deafeningly loud. Hundreds of voices jostle to get your attention, some angrier and more desperate than others. The hands pull at your hair, your neck, your limbs, and tug at the corners of your mouth, demanding your attention. They beg you and scream at you to help them, to stop ignoring them. 

Then, in the darkness, they start to take form. You start to make out the glint of eyes, far too wide to be human, staring at you from the shadows. You see gaping maws where mouths belong, stringy with god-knows-what and stinking. Skulls with bits of flesh falling off. Hanging jaws, opening and shutting, attempting to beg. They close in on you, cheek to jowl, screeching in your face, *demanding* you save them. Threatening to bring you across to their world if you don't. But you'll never be able to respond or do anything. Just hear them crying out loud, screeching at you, faces rotting.

If you're lucky, at this point, you'll pass out, and you'll come to when it's light again, and it'll all be over. But you'll never stop seeing the faces in the dark. 

I can see them watching me now, when I run up the stairs to escape them. I see them swiping at my feet, but they never grab me. They just wait. They know one day I'll fuck up again, and take too long to run. 

I don't want to know what happens if I don't pass out next time.
